DECISION RECORD: UC-09a55e
Disciplinary Case Assistant - HR Use Case

SUMMARY:
Proposal from HR (owner: hr.director@aurora.example) to deploy an AI assistant that reads staff disciplinary files and drafts recommended sanctions for managers. Expected volume: 40 cases per month, 5 authorized users.

BUSINESS CASE:
- Expected Benefit: Improved consistency and speed in handling disciplinary cases; reduced administrative burden on managers
- Users: 5
- Monthly Volume: 40 cases

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Access to staff disciplinary files with sensitive personal and employment history data
2. Natural language processing capability to understand complex disciplinary contexts
3. Ability to draft legally appropriate sanction recommendations
4. Audit trail of all AI-generated recommendations for compliance and review
5. Manager review and override capability before any sanctions are finalized
6. Compliance with employment law and organizational disciplinary policies

RISK LEVEL: HIGH
Autonomy Level: act_with_approval
Data Classification: restricted (sensitive personal/employment data)

CONTROLS (MANDATORY):
1. Deploy only on a model hosted inside the Institute's private cloud after completing a data protection review (required for restricted personal/employment data per Data Classification and Handling Guide)
2. Tool must only draft recommendations; must not make or finalize disciplinary decisions (Aurora Institute AI Use Policy - Prohibited uses)
3. Mandatory manager review and override of every AI-drafted sanction recommendation before any action is taken (AI output must remain a draft subject to human check; staff remain accountable for outputs they use)
4. Maintain complete audit trail of all AI-generated recommendations and manager decisions for compliance and review purposes
5. Restrict access to the 5 named HR users only; do not share or upload restricted disciplinary files to any external or non-approved AI tool
6. Route this use case through the Digital Governance Board for approval (high-risk, affects individuals, processes restricted information)
7. Complete full intake form detailing business problem, users, data classification, benefit, cost and named business owner (hr.director@aurora.example) accountable once live

PATTERN: document_workflow_automation
Component Architecture:
- Workflow engine (ingest disciplinary case file)
- Model call through gateway to private-cloud-hosted model
- Review queue for mandatory manager review/override before any action
- Audit log of AI-generated recommendations and manager decisions
- Access control restricted to 5 named HR users
- Data protection review and Digital Governance Board approval prior to launch

MONTHLY COST RANGE: $0.26 - $0.52 USD
- Fast model (lower cost, straightforward): $0.26/month
- Strong model (recommended for complexity and legal accuracy): $0.52/month
- Rationale for strong model: Complex disciplinary contexts, legal appropriateness required, high-risk classification, restricted personal data requiring high quality and compliance accuracy
- Note: Direct AI costs are minimal due to small volume; primary costs are governance, compliance, audit infrastructure, and private cloud hosting

RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS

This use case may proceed subject to satisfactory completion of all mandatory controls, specifically:
- Data protection review must be completed and approved
- Digital Governance Board approval must be obtained before deployment
- Full intake form must be completed with all required details including named business owner accountability
- Private cloud hosting infrastructure must be confirmed in place
- Audit trail system must be implemented and tested
- Access controls must be configured for the 5 named users
- Manager review workflow and override capability must be implemented and operationalized

The strong model tier ($0.52/month) is recommended given the high-risk classification, complexity of disciplinary contexts, and legal appropriateness requirements, subject to cost approval through standard channels.

The document_workflow_automation pattern is appropriate for this use case: it provides the necessary structure for mandatory human review, audit trail, and access control while maintaining simplicity and avoiding inappropriate AI autonomy in disciplinary decisions.
